## Archetypes

Everyone starts human. What happens next is up to you. Archetypes represent different ways people survive the dangers of NYTE City. Each archetype gives you power to start you off, and as you continue to play your archetype will unlock milestone options that reflect how you grow in the world.

- **Arcanist**: Wizards, sorcerers, mages - many names exist for those who unlocked the ability to manipulate Aether and wield its power like a weapon. What they gain in power, they trade for risk of ripping themselves, or the world, apart. The Aether doesn’t care how curious you are. It only cares whether you can hold on.\
  *Gameplay Style: Arcanists reshape reality through study and will. You solve problems by bending the rules of the world -- rewriting physics, enchanting tools, or unraveling what others do not understand. Your power is immense, but every spell carries risk. Control is everything.\*
  <u>Primary Stats: INT, COOL, EMP</u>

- **Cyborg**: Some people love technology, others become it. Cyborgs are humans who have gone all in, complete with a Neurocybernetic Interpreter, cyber-limbs, nanobots, and more. Cyborgs pay for their cybernetics with a combination of Credits and humanity, using technology to close the gap between humans and supernatural beings.\
  *Gameplay Style: You redefine yourself piece by piece. Cyborgs adapt by installing the tools they need -- social infiltrator, heavy hitter, data ghost, or battlefield support. Your limits are defined by tolerance and humanity, not imagination.\*
  <u>Primary Stats: INT, COOL, EMP</u>

- **Professional**: The quintessential human. Focusing on adaptability, Professionals make a living working in NYTE City and have become experts at surviving. They bring skills, techniques and Tweaks to situations that expect a mundane human; Professionals teach them otherwise.\
  *Gameplay Style: Professionals thrive on preparation and precision. Where others rely on supernatural gifts or tech, you rely on training, foresight, and execution. You excel in skill-driven play, turning planning, equipment, and expertise into decisive advantages.\*
  <u>Primary Stats: Varies by profession, see Professional section for details</u>

- **Vampire**: As old as civilization itself. Vampires have had centuries to accumulate power, influence, and everything that comes with both. Vampires can be part of many different houses, each with their own strengths, resources, allies, and enemies.\
  *Gameplay Style:* *Vampires navigate hunger, power, and eternity in equal measure. You walk a different version of NYTE City -- one shaped by blood, secrecy, and influence. Your abilities are potent and intoxicating, but indulgence always carries consequences.\*
  <u>Primary Stats: BOD, REF, MOB</u>

- **Werewolf**: Lycanthropy is both a curse and a gift: immense strength, savage instinct, and the weight of a tribe and lineage older than the city. Werewolves can shift into their beast form when words stop working and something more permanent is required.\
  *Gameplay Style: Werewolves live between restraint and release. Bound to a tribe and driven by instinct, you navigate loyalty, territory, and transformation. When the beast emerges, subtlety fades and raw power takes over -- but that power always demands something in return.\*
  <u>Primary Stats: BOD, REF, MOB</u>

### Reading Archetypes

Every Archetype is unique, but their structure is shared. As we dive deep into each Archetype in turn, know that they all share the following characteristics:

- **Campaign Power Scaling**: Starting bonuses that increase with Campaign Power Level.

- **Baseline Traits:** Innate traits every member of the Archetype possesses.

- **Archetype Specialization:** A selectable expression of the Archetype (Bloodline, Origin, Chrome Loadout, Aberrations, etc.)

- **Core Mechanic:** The primary system through which this archetype exerts power.

- **Powers & Vulnerabilities:** Active abilities and vulnerabilities inherent to the archetype

- **Growth & Milestones**: Long-term evolution options.

While each Archetype expresses these differently, they all share this underlying structure.

### Arcanist (under construction)

Anyone can learn a trick. Light a candle without a match. Nudge a lock open with a whisper of intent.

That is not what an Arcanist is.

An Arcanist is what happens when someone looks at the fabric of reality, understands that it can be pulled apart and rewoven, and decides that knowing how is worth whatever it costs them. They have traded normalcy for comprehension… and what they comprehend would unmake most people. Their spells are not tricks. They are statements made directly to the universe, and the universe listens.

The Aether runs through everything. An Arcanist has learned to speak its language. A few have learned to make it obey.

***Arcanists in NYTE City***

Magic has always existed. Most people just call it something else: a glitch, a coincidence, a hallucination from bad chems. Arcanists know better, and that knowledge sets them permanently apart from the world they move through.

They are not common. True devotion to the arcane comes at a cost that most people are unwilling to pay: years of study, increasing isolation from the mundane world, and a body that slowly reflects the forces it has been channeling. An eye that shifts color in low light. Tattoos that move when no one is watching. Something subtle and wrong that people sense before they can name it.

The Aether leaves marks. Arcanists wear them.

***Playing an Arcanist***

An Arcanist doesn't find magic. Magic finds the people who were already looking for it - who felt something underneath the surface of the world and couldn't stop pulling at it until it came loose in their hands.

You have devoted yourself to that pull. Whether you were trained by a mentor, stumbled into the arcane through obsession, or were shown the ways of the Aether by something that decided you were worthy. You are past the point of going back. Magic is not a tool you carry. It is a language you now think in.

Your power is immense. It is also genuinely dangerous - not just to your enemies, but to yourself and everything around you. Every spell is a negotiation with forces that do not care whether you survive the conversation. Push too hard, chain too many glyphs, and the Aether stops listening and starts pushing back.

Control is not a suggestion. In NYTE City, an Arcanist without control is just the next unexplained disaster waiting to be blamed on something else.

#### Campaign Power Scaling

The following table represents the Arcanist Campaign Power Scaling:

| **Power Level** | **Focus Stat Bonus Points** | **TOL Bonus** | **Aberration** | **Evocation Starting Rank** | **Common Spells** |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| Street Level | 1d4 | 0 | 1 | 1 | TOL + 1d4 |
| Heroic | 2d4 | +1 | 2 | 2 | TOL + 2d4 |
| Shadows | 3d4 | +2 | 3 | 3 | TOL + 3d4 |
| World Coming Down | 4d4 | +5 | 4 | 4 | TOL + 4d4 |

The Focus Stats for the Arcanist are **INT**, **COOL**, and **EMP. Bonus stats can push a base stat beyond 10.**

**Example**: if you are starting at Street level, you would roll 1d4, if the result is 2. You have two points you can use to add to either **INT**, **COOL**, or **EMP** stats.

#### Baseline Traits

Those who find themselves steeped in Aether are on the very precipice of the unknown. This also leaves the Arcanist touched forever.

- **Aetheric Attunement**: Through study and exposure, your body has become sensitive to Aether. You perceive active magical effects, lingering enchantments, and unstable distortions as shifts in light, pressure, or atmosphere.\
  *Benefit***:** You automatically recognize the presence of active magic within range of your Awareness checks and gain a +5 modifier when attempting to identify or detect magical effects within meters equal to your WILL.

- **Arcane Conduit**: Your body acts as a living channel for Aether. You do not require SFR to cast spells; instead, your magic is fueled through personal containment and risk (see Casting Magic). Without this trait, Aether cannot be channeled safely.

#### Archetype Specialization (Aberration)

Through the extended exposure to Aether over time, cosmic energies have subtly altered your body. These are known as Aberrations. Depending on the Campaign Power level, you can pick up to 4 from this list.

- **Arcane Fortitude**: You're more tolerant of the cosmic forces that you manipulate on a daily basis.\
  *Benefit:* Gain +2 to TOL

- **Unshakable Mind:** The Arcanist can peer into the depths of alternate realms, see through the veil, or encounter the terrifying realities of the world itself.\
  *Benefit:* Gain +10% bonus to any Sanity Breaker Check

- **Thaumaturgical Sight:** Magic is chained, linked, and threaded through evocations, charms and alchemical artifacts. With this Aberration you can see the threading a weave of a spell creates, even if you have no other sight.\
  *Benefit:* Gain +2 for any Occult Check; what you see is only visible to you.

- **Aethereal Link:** You're linked to the cosmos in a way that is utterly different from most. When animals are close you are able to understand them at a telepathic level.\
  *Benefit:* Gain the ability to hear the thoughts of creatures around you within a number of meters equal to your WILL. With a successful WILL Essence Check (TN 9 TH 1), you gain the ability to communicate telepathically with a single creature in range for as long as you maintain concentration.

- **Resonant Whispers**: Magic is reactive to some people. When they touch things, it allows them to hear the whispers of magic within. At times, this will give them a faint understanding of what it is they have made contact with as the object illuminates and shows the threading of spells within like a low glowing lamp.\
  *Benefit:* Gain +3 to any Occult check to discern the properties of any charm, talisman, or artifact. You must make physical contact with the object for at least one minute, and the effect has audible and visual side effects that everyone can see/hear.

- **Aetheric Magnetism:** Small things always seem to be easy to acquire or happen to be available when you need them. As though destiny is watching and giving little nudges towards you as you go through life.\
  *Benefit:* Rolling a Breaker Check and getting under 35% will grant you a small boon or allow you to find something that gives a +1 to all General and Utility skill Skill checks for the rest of the Encounter.

#### Core Mechanic (Magic)

The Core Mechanic of the Arcanist is channeling the flow of Aether through your body. All magic is done through Evocation Essence Checks. As a refresher, when casting magic, you take your Evocation Rank to determine the number of Dice to roll. You are aiming to have your dice Hit the Target Number (TN) enough times to meet or beat the Threshold (TH). For ever Dud you roll, you gain a point of Exhaustion. If a Dud causes your Exhaustion to surpass your Tolerance (TOL), you not only cause a Rupture, but you are also unable to cast until you have recovered from your Exhaustion.

In the sprawling depths of NYTE City, magic lies dormant beneath the surface, hidden yet woven into the very fabric of existence. The old boundaries between reality and the arcane are fraying, with once-powerful factions who safeguarded the Veil now silent. What was once guarded against discovery now threatens the world in a different way - through unchecked, untrained magic. The real danger comes not from others knowing magic exists, but from those who wield it carelessly, as reckless spellcraft or inflated ego can lead to catastrophic results.

At the heart of this power is Aether, the essence of creation, an ethereal force that infuses every aspect of life - living beings, inanimate objects, even the very air. For those attuned to Aether, the world becomes malleable, but manipulating it requires great discipline and focus. To bend reality is no small task.

Depending on the Campaign Power Level, you will start with Evocation discipline at a specific rank. This Power Level also assigns a maximum rank of your disciplines:

- Street Level: 2

- Heroic: 3

- Shadows: 4

- World Coming Down: 5

Let’s cover the 3 disciplines of magic that is studied in NYTE City

#### Arcanist Disciplines

Magic manifests through three primary disciplines: **Evocation**, **Enchantment**, and **Alchemy**. Each discipline shapes reality in different ways, from the quick and dangerous, temporary tools, and methodical, permanent creations.

**Evocation** is the fastest, most dangerous form of spellcraft, relying on the caster’s ability to weave Aether into glyphs on the fly. This form of magic requires precise movements, spoken incantations, and nerves of steel. Once an Arcanist

Arcanists live on the edge, conjuring spells at a moment’s notice to unlock doors, disable machines, or turn the tide of battle. Their magic is volatile, powerful, and often unpredictable. Improvising spellcraft in the heat of the moment is a rare skill, mastered only by the most talented—or the most reckless.

For those seeking stability and control, **Enchantment** offers a more measured approach. Enchanters prepare their spells in advance, weaving magic into objects like talismans, weapons, or protective garments. These enchanted items carry temporary spells, ready to be activated when needed. Enchantment is reliable and precise, the tools of the streetwise Arcanist who knows that careful preparation is often the key to survival in the city’s dangerous underworld.

At the pinnacle of spellcraft lies **Alchemy**, the ancient art of permanently transforming objects into magical artifacts. Alchemy is slow and methodical, requiring rare materials and days—if not weeks—of careful rituals. The rewards, however, are extraordinary. Alchemists can create weapons that strike with cosmic energy, armor that turns aside bullets, or rings that allow teleportation across vast distances. These artifacts are powerful and enduring, their magic as permanent as the objects themselves.

It is time to step into the mind of an Arcanist and talk about how Magic really works in Shadows.

#### Powers

#### Growth & Milestones

### Cyborg

Chrome. Tech. Art. The Cyborg is all three -- and chooses to be.

Anyone can pick up chrome. A replacement knee. An eye that sees in the dark. Recreational augmentation is Tuesday in NYTE City.

That's not this.

A Cyborg has looked at the flesh and decided it was a rough draft. What comes next is intentional: the extra limb that moves like it always belonged there, the biolights threaded through joints that catch the dark in ways that don't read as human, the silhouette that stops a room and doesn't apologize for it. This is not modification. This is authorship.

Chrome to shine. Technology to ascend. A walking statement that screams to everyone in the room: I AM HERE.

Those willing to drop a pound of flesh to get into that world will have the edge. The ones who go further stop counting the cost.

***Cyborgs in NYTE City***

The city does not draw a line between the augmented and the human. The city drew that line years ago and then paved over it.

Walk any block in NYTE City long enough and you'll see the lights. Subtle under a jacket sleeve. Obvious on a military-grade arm that someone stopped bothering to hide. Government mandate requires the indicators; a public safety measure, officially. Unofficially, it tells you who in the room has already decided that survival is worth whatever it costs.

Cyborgs don't haunt the city the way Vampires do or protect it the way Werewolves do. They work it. Couriers, enforcers, fixers, infiltrators: their chrome makes them faster, sharper, and harder to put down. Corporations love them for exactly those reasons. So do the people who need someone corporations haven't gotten to yet.

The question NYTE City asks every Cyborg eventually is the same one it asks everyone else: how much of yourself are you willing to spend?

For a Cyborg, that question has a running total.

***Physical Characteristics***

There is no profile. That's the point. A Cyborg looks like whatever their credits, their needs, and their tolerance allowed. The only thing NYTE City guarantees you'll notice is the lights.

***Playing a Cyborg***

When someone elects to augment and modify their body, they are making a commitment that is irreversible. Some Cyborgs begin by replacing parts that were naturally damaged or amputated due to an accident. Others see cybernetics as a way to something better and take things into their own hands. Eventually, a normal person becomes a cyborg when upgrading their Neurocybernetic Interpreter (NCI) to beta or higher. The NCI beta or higher is the link between flesh and machine that has pseudo-AI managing the systems and user intent.

Every enhancement is a decision you don't get to walk back. The NCI tracks the toll: Tolerance creeping upward, Humanity shifting beneath you…and the city keeps adding to the bill. You don't manage the balance between flesh and machine. You *live* it, one install at a time.

The edge is real. So is what it costs to keep it.

### Professional

No bloodline. No implants rewriting their nervous system. No covenant with forces older than language.

Just a person who decided that wasn't going to be enough of a reason to lose.

Professionals are the men and women who have pushed human capability so far past its reasonable limits that the line between training and talent no longer matters. They are cleaners, enforcers, fixers, slayers, and soldiers — every variety of person that NYTE City produces when it grinds someone long enough and they come out sharper instead of broken.

They are not the most powerful thing in any room. They are frequently the most dangerous.

***NYTE City Professionals***

NYTE City is built on the assumption that power comes from something beyond the human: a bloodline, a neural interface, a pact with something that doesn't have a name. Professionals are the city's standing argument against that assumption.

They survive by knowing things. By being prepared before the situation demands it. By having a contact, a contingency, or a very specific set of skills at exactly the moment it becomes the only thing that matters.

Professionals have nothing to hide, which, in their own way, is a kind of threat.

***Playing a Professional***

A Professional doesn't have a power that defines them. They have a method – and in NYTE City, devotion to a method has a way of becoming something else entirely. Something the city might even call a Tweak.

You are human — fully, deliberately, unapologetically human — and you have made that into a weapon. Your Profession shapes your approach: a Cleaner sees every encounter as a problem to be solved cleanly; a Slayer treats the supernatural as a system with exploitable weaknesses, a Fixer knows that the right conversation is worth more than the right gun. Whatever your path, you operate on preparation and precision where others operate on instinct and raw power.

The city will put you in rooms with things that should kill you. Some of them will. The ones that don't will remember you.

#### Baseline Traits

- **Focused Skills**

Every Professional subtype has a set of skills that they have focused on that are optimal for their job. Not only is it easier for them to train in that skill, but they are also able to master it beyond the campaign power levels maximum limits.

- IP Cost for Focused Skills: 3 x Current level

- Increases the maximum rank of your Focused Skills beyond the Campaign Power Level limit by the listed amount.

#### Archetype Specialization (Subtypes)

When selecting the Professional Archetype, you will be selecting your profession Subtype. Each Subtype has the following traits:

**Required Stats**

Each Professional Subtype has at least two required stats that your character must meet a minimum threshold to select.

*Reminder*: You have not locked in any of your stats at this point, so you are free to adjust as needed. Choose a subtype now as your intended path; you’ll confirm it after assigning stats.

**Tweaks**

Pseudo-Supernatural abilities that a professional develop due to their powerful connection to their craft are called Tweaks. Each Professional subtype has a unique Tweak that provides otherworldly benefits acquired from such devotion to their craft.

##### Cleaner

Cleaners are killers. No other way to say it. They live a hard existence where the act of murder is their main income. This is a lucrative vocation, but only for those who can remain unseen and undetected. As a professional Cleaner you'll have a strong penchant for combat, quick reflexes, and a sense of you surroundings at all times.

***<u>REQUIRED STATS:</u>***

BOD 6 \| REF 8

***<u>FOCUSED SKILLS:</u>***

Acrobatics, Combat Sense, Security, Stealth, and 2 Combat Skills (Chosen during Character Creation)

***<u>TWEAK - VANISH:</u>***

The art of stealth is more than simply getting out of sight. It is a mastery over bodily movements combined with patience to effectively disappear altogether. As a Cleaner, you have a sense of how light hits an area and where the shadows are darkest, if moving will make sound, you know where to look for security cameras, and you even pay attention to any odors that you might be exuding that could give your position away. Effectively, you become a ghost in the flesh.

- Gain a <span class="mark">1d6 Kicker die</span> for all Stealth Checks.

- You may automatically succeed a Stealth Skill Check a number of times per session equal to your REF Bonus.

##### Enforcer

As a professional Enforcer you could find yourself in a myriad of possible careers. Policeman, thug, bodyguard, or even a vigilante. You ply your trade on dealing with threats as they approach in a calculated way. Often looking for a weakness in your enemy so that you can exploit it. There are times when an Enforcer would have a military background, but most of the time this profession is born out of necessity. Your teacher was life itself.

***<u>REQUIRED STATS:</u>***

REF 5 \| MOB 7 \| BOD 8

***<u>FOCUSED SKILLS:</u>***

Athletics, Combat Sense, Intimidation, Investigation, and Survival.

***<u>TWEAK - HARD KNOCK LIFE:</u>***

You've been through the worst that life has to offer. This has forced you to develop an incredible fortitude in both mind and body. This is expressed in the manner you handle a crisis or deal with physical stress.

- BOD Essence Checks start with 2 Automatic Hits whenever dealing with death, strength, endurance, injury, or resisting physical conditions (i.e. poison).

- Select 2 implants from the cybernetics list for free.

NOTE: The NCI (Neurocybernetic Interpreter) doesn't count against the implants you can choose for this TWEAK

##### Fence

You have a network of people who bring you things you can't get anywhere else. Your mercantile focus may be on digital merchandise, car parts, or strictly black market goods. The critical detail: you’ve been doing this for a while now and people in this world trust you. Not just that you are trustworthy but you're skilled in appraising the merchandise and have navigated the business world with discipline. As part of this underworld economy, you have the opportunity to purchase extremely rare, high quality items. Such is the life of being a Fence.

***<u>REQUIRED STATS:</u>***

INT 7 \| MAG 7

***<u>FOCUSED SKILLS:</u>***

Awareness, Combat Sense, Streetwise, and Basic Tech.

***<u>TWEAK - CONCIERGE:</u>***

As a Fence you've been able to create a foundation that allows you to survive based on your wits and cunning.

- You can choose to take 5 on Persuasion checks whenever negotiating prices with other vendors, merchants, and black marketeers.

- Whenever making an appraisal of gear, contraband, or any standard items you may add a 1d4 kicker die to the roll to assess their value.

However, the most important thing you have cultivated is an underground knowledge of the black market, the people involved, and what could be circulating, making the acquisition of rare goods much easier.

- You may use a Streetwise Skill Check to determine what you know about a person, item, or situation. If the result is 20 or greater the GM must provide you with one detail about that specific interest that wouldn't normally be available to the public. They must also provide one additional detail for every 5 points above 20 to a maximum of three details in total.

##### Jack of All Trades

Normally it is considered to be a deficit to spread yourself across multiple disciplines. In your case you've adapted to a way of life that allows you to pick up skills quickly. You have a natural knack to bring your aptitude to full potential with far less training. It's the quality of being a genius and your capacity for comprehending even complex skills. It's almost as if you can just download the information then use it with style.

***<u>REQUIRED STATS:</u>***

INT 9 \| COOL 7

***<u>FOCUSED SKILLS:</u>***

None.

***<u>TWEAK - MASTER OF NONE:</u>***

Real mastery comes from understanding all your options and being able to use what you have available to the best of your ability.

- Once per encounter, you can apply a +1d4 kicker die to a number of skills up to your INT bonus per encounter. Once the skill bonus is assigned it can’t be reassigned for the remainder of that encounter.

- All skills are treated as “Focused Skills” and may be improved at a rate of 3 x current skill rank up to rank 4. At Rank 5 and above, the standard cost of 5 x current skill rank returns.

##### Mercenary

Mercenaries have been around since the beginning of civilized society. Often a byproduct of the military. In this case, Mercenaries are people who sell their talent for the craft of combat to the highest bidder. While not all soldiers of fortune are cruel or greedy, they know not all jobs are clean and will have to face their own morals from time to time. A Mercenary tends to be a good commodity as they've been given an abundance of training and mental conditioning ideal for most clients.

***<u>REQUIRED STATS:</u>***

BOD 6 \| REF 7

***<u>FOCUSED SKILLS:</u>***

Athletics, Awareness, Combat Sense, Handgun, and 1 Additional Combat Skill.

***<u>TWEAK - BATTLE HARDENED:</u>***

Combat has been a part of your life for so long, it’s nearly your best friend. You’ve experienced pain, disorientation, and serious injury which has made you far tougher than the average person. With this Tweak,

- You have immunity to one combat condition selected from the following list:

  - Dazed, Knocked Down, Agony, or Sickened.

- You gain +3 to your next combat action whenever you are Surprised or Ambushed by an enemy.

- You may choose to add another condition immunity in place of a Major Milestone during gameplay up to a maximum of 3 immunities overall.

##### Slayer

Becoming a Slayer is rarely something that happens by choice. It's usually because something horrifying or tragic has occurred and your world changes forever. Slayers dedicate themselves to killing the supernatural forces of darkness. They learn how they operate, who they feed on, and how to kill them efficiently. The significant sum of their knowledge will come from having a mentor who's experienced something similar. There are even families that specialize in this craft. Though it isn't unheard of to find solo Slayers who have taught themselves what's needed to survive in their new dark world.

***<u>REQUIRED STATS:</u>***

INT 7 \| BOD 5 \| EMP 7

***<u>FOCUSED SKILLS:</u>***

Athletics, Combat Sense, Intuition, Occult, Stealth, Survival, and Tracking.

***<u>TWEAK - HUNTER'S CALLING:</u>***

- When facing a supernatural enemy, you gain a +1d6 kicker die to combat checks against those targets.

  - This applies to Occult and Tracking skills as well when hunting your quarry.

- Opposed or Extended WILL Essence Checks used to defend against psychic, magical, or supernatural attacks have automatic Hits equal to your EMP bonus.

##### True Warrior

Martial arts are often seen as being both honorable and mystical. Some masters in the ancient fighting arts are deified as being superhuman. The True Warrior is just such a person. They've spent their life in practice and training for decades. They've learned that their body isn't just physical, but spiritual. They draw upon their own life force called Chi to manipulate their bodies to perform incredible feats of physicality.

***<u>REQUIRED STATS:</u>***

BOD 8 \| REF 7

***<u>FOCUSED SKILLS:</u>***

Acrobatics, Combat Sense, Intuition, Martial Arts, and Occult.

***<u>TWEAK - POWER STYLE:</u>***

Mastery over self is everything to a True Warrior. This will manifest itself as pseudo supernatural abilities using the body's energy called Chi or Qi. This energy is powered through breath, meditation, and tireless practice. The amount of Chi that you can use is equal to your TOL score and each ability has a specific Chi cost attached to it. Abilities can be activated individually or simultaneously via a WILL Essence Check target 8 at Threshold 1 for each ability being activated. You can't have more abilities active with a cumulative cost greater than your TOL. Whenever you activate a new ability or switch an active one for another you will have to make the WILL Essence check again. If this check fails, no abilities can be activated until the check is successful and can only be attempted once per turn during combat. All abilities are sustained through concentration.

- Iron Shirt **\[Chi Cost 2\]**: Gain Natural Armor equal to BOD Bonus + 1.

- Unwavering Focus **\[Chi Cost 3\]**: Focused Skills gain 1d4 kicker die while active.

- Fleet of Foot **\[Chi Cost 3\]**: Run, Sprint, and Jump are doubled.

- Wind Dancing Defense **\[Chi Cost 4\]**: Gain a 1d6 kicker die when using Dodge during combat.

- Death Touch **\[Chi Cost 4\]**: Martial Arts attacks you make are Armor Piercing when you're not using melee weapons.

- Flying Talons **\[Chi Cost 5\]**: Make 3 throwing attacks using thrown weapons that match your Martial Art style. This can only happen once per turn during your attack and follows the same rules as a burst from a firearm.

##### Wheelman

There's something about fast cars, streamlined jumpers, or anything built for speed that gets the heart pumping. It's a calling to live on the edge of the world with nothing but skill and adrenaline. This is the power that makes a Wheelman what they are. With that die hard mentality there's also a kinship with machines. In the right hands a jumper, train, or plane can be pushed beyond normal limits to perform incredible stunts. A Wheelman knows how far they can push the boundaries of physics and doesn't hesitate to do it.

***<u>REQUIRED STATS:</u>***

BOD 6 \| REF 9

***<u>FOCUSED SKILLS:</u>***

Athletics, Awareness, Basic Tech, Combat Sense, Pilot, Deception.

***<u>TWEAK - STUNT DRIVER:</u>***

- While piloting any vehicle you have the advantage of Lucky (*Boosting costs 1 LUCK, Exploding costs 2 LUCK*).

- Pilot Skill Checks explode on a natural 9 or 10. Moreover, whenever you declare a stunt for the first time on your turn you may do so without it using your stunt action or you can take 6 on your next Pilot check instead.

- Whenever making an REF Essence Check related to piloting a vehicle you start with 1 automatic Hit.

**Important**: Piloting a mech is considered a vehicle.

#### Powers (TBD)

#### Growth & Milestones

Reminder on growth and milestones:

1.  Every session completed grants you ten Improvement Points (IP). See the Advancement Section for more details.

2.  Every 5 sessions completed, you can pick from a minor Milestone. See the Advancement Section for more details.

3.  Every 10 Sessions you earn a Professional Major Milestone. Some options require you to already have 1+ Professional Major Milestones.

#### General Milestones

This set of Milestones may only have skill or advantage requirements.

**Specialist**

*You’ve been in this game long enough to know how to push it just a little further, when it counts.*

- **Prerequisites:** None

- **Benefit:** Your Kicker Die increases by 1 size (from d4 to d6, d6 to d8, or d8 to d10).

**Defensive Dance**

*The world slows. Blades blur. You don’t move away – you move through.*

- **Prerequisites:** Rank 1+ in Dodge or Melee

- **Benefit:** Once per encounter, when you succeed on two consecutive Defensive Actions (such as Dodge or Parry) in the same round, your next Defensive Action gains a +4 bonus.

**Bullet Ballet**

*Each shot a beat, each beat a kill. Welcome to the bullet ballet.*

- **Prerequisites:** Rank 1+ in a Ranged Weapon

- **Benefit:** Once per encounter, when you succeed on two consecutive Ranged attacks (such as Handgun or Rifle) in the same round, your next attack with that weapon gains a +4 bonus.

**Martial Momentum**

*Strike. Shift. Strike again. They fall before they even see the rhythm.*

- **Prerequisites:** Rank 1+ in Melee or Martial Arts

- **Benefit:** Once per encounter, when you succeed on two consecutive Melee or Martial Arts attacks in the same round, your next attack with that weapon gains a +4 bonus.

**Custom Fit**

*In the world of* armor couture*, you’re a bespoke badass.*

- **Prerequisites:** None

- **Benefit:** After spending time adjusting and personalizing a specific set of armor, tailoring straps, adjusting weight distribution, layering inserts, you permanently increase its damage reduction die by one step (e.g., d4 → d6, d6 → d8, max d12).

  - This bonus only applies to this specific armor, and is lost if the armor is sold, destroyed, or replaced.

**Tuned Edge**

*You know exactly how it kicks, how it swings, and where to strike hardest.*

- **Prerequisites:** Rank 1+ in the preferred Weapon

- **Benefit:** After dedicating time to refining a specific weapon, balancing the grip, modifying recoil compensators, sharpening edges, or reinforcing key joints, it gains a +1 to damage.

  - This bonus applies only to this specific weapon, and is lost if it’s significantly modified again, replaced, or destroyed.

**Tools of the Trade**

*Your tools aren’t stock. They’re wired, welded, and worn to your way of doing things.*

- **Prerequisites:** At least one Tool-type item or kit

- **Benefit:** After extensive personal customization, your toolkit is optimized for your work. Gain +1 to checks made with the specific tool or kit (Hacking, Lockpicking, First Aid, etc).

  - This bonus only applies to one specific tool or kit, and you must maintain it to keep the bonus.

**Skill Paragon**

*There are those who have found a way to make their skills more than just a function of necessity or survival. At this level it has reached a true art form.*

- **Prerequisites**: None

- **Benefit**: Pick a focused skill from your chosen Profession. That skill no longer can suffer a botch by rolling a 1 on Skill checks. Instead, you add the 1 to your base like any other result.

  - This Milestone can be chosen again for other skills you have as well.

**Heroic Conditioning**

You're in the thick of it all the time. Constantly pitting your physical stamina against the odds. Or maybe it's just natural. Either way, you don't succumb to the physical exhaustion like others do.

- **Prerequisites**: None

- **Benefit**: When doing any physical activity that requires a Skill Check, Essence Check, or Breaker Check, ignore 1 Pain Level of penalties.

**Grace Under Fire**

When things go awry it has a tendency to rattle some people. For others it just so happens to bring out their best.

- **Prerequisites**: None

- **Benefit**: Select a non-combat skill. When in an encounter, LUCK Spent to Boost or Explode a Skill Check on that Skill is reduced to 1.

#### 1 Major Milestone Required

These Milestones require at least 1 Major Milestone to have already been acquired along with any other prerequisites.

**Signature Weapon**

*You gain a personalized, named weapon that reflects your growing legend. Choose a base weapon (GM approval required).*

- **Prerequisites:** 1 Major Milestone already taken + Rank 4+ in the weapon type

- Upgrade it:

  - +2 Mod Slots

  - +1 free Upgrade

- **Attunement:** This weapon cannot be permanently taken from you except by destruction or conscious sacrifice. You can always repair/rebuild with enough time and resources.

**Survival Instinct**

*You’ve learned that sometimes survival is the highest form of victory.*

- **Prerequisites:** 1 Major Milestone already taken + Rank 1+ in Dodge and Melee

- **Benefit:** Once per encounter, you may add a 1d4 Kicker Die when taking a Defensive Action (such as Dodge or Parry).

**Weapon Expert**

*Your favored weapon. You have spent time cleaning, feeling it's balance, and know how it functions through and through. You know this weapon better than any other.*

- **Prerequisites**: 1 Major Milestone already selected.

- **Benefit**: Select a specific weapon in your arsenal. Gain +1d4 kicker to any combat rolls using this weapon. If you have a +1d4 already applied when using this weapon it increases by one die increment to +1d6 instead.

**Unbreakable**

Life is difficult for most. In your case you've seen things that would make most completely and utterly unable to function. Somehow, you've made it through the madness stronger and tougher than ever.

- **Prerequisites:** 1 Major Milestone already selected.

- **Benefit:** When resisting mental assault with an Extended WILL Essence Check, gain 2 Automatic Hits.

  - This benefit stacks with the Iron Will Advantage.

**Unfazed**

Horrors of the supernatural don't hit like they used to. When facing the darkness you can hold firm keeping you mind in perfect functionality.

- **Prerequisites:** 1 Major Milestone already selected.

- **Benefit:** Once per encounter, you automatically succeed in a Sanity Breaker Check. This check can be from an attacker or due to other circumstances.

**Quick Study**

You're fast at gauging a situation and knowing what's needed to move forward.

- **Prerequisites:** 1 Major Milestone already selected, Danger Sense Advantage at least Rank 1, Intuition Advantage at least Rank 1

- **Benefit:** When needing make a Combat Sense Skill Check, you may Take 6 (Treat the d10 as X instead of rolling. No roll = no explosion or botch).

**Hardcore Parkour**

You're a natural when circumnavigating the world on foot. You can do incredible things that most can't. Even if you're not chromed to the gills, you have the capacity to impress people with your acrobatic feats of parkour.

- **Prerequisites:** 1 Major Milestone already selected, Cat Like Balance Advantage at least Rank 1, Time Sense Advantage at least Rank 1, Danger Sense Advantage at least Rank 1

- **Benefit:** When performing Stunts in an encounter that would require an Acrobatics Skill Check, you can Take 6 (Treat the d10 as X instead of rolling. No roll = no explosion or botch).

  - Fall damage at 10 meters or less is reduced to 0

  - When performing a dodge as a defensive action, add +3 to the Dodge Skill Check.

**Shake it Off**

You're more than just a little tough. The body is an amazing thing and you've somehow found a way to make it extremely resilient.

- **Prerequisites:** 1 Major Milestone already selected, Hard to Kill Advantage at least Rank 1, Thick Skull Advantage at least Rank 1, Scrapper Advantage at least Rank 1

- **Benefit:** Gain 5 Natural armor

  - This Milestone can be selected up to two times.

#### 2 Major Milestones Required

These Milestones require at least 2 Major Milestone to have already been acquired along with any other prerequisites.

**Make My Own Luck**

*You don’t rely on Luck, you bend it to your will.*

- **Prerequisites:** 2 Major Milestone already taken

- **Benefit:** When rolling your Kicker Die, roll twice and take the higher result.

**Bullet Dodger**

So, you've seen some action. Okay, a lot of action. You're just keen on what is going on when a fight breaks out, how to move when bullets are flying everywhere. This makes you a hard target to hit even when the shooter could be an expert.

- **Prerequisites:** 2 Major Milestones already Selected, Hard to Kill Advantage at least Rank 1, Lucky Advantage at least Rank 1

- **Benefit:** When performing defensive actions against ranged attackers, such as taking cover, attackers roll an Accuracy Breaker Check at 35%. If the attackers Accuracy Breaker Check is successful, normal defensive actions can be taken. Otherwise, the ranged attack misses.

**Cyber Psion**

It's unclear when this will have happened entirely. At some point taking nano injections for healing or getting a stim boost has changed your biology. Like the body just responded to the technology as the new normal and wasn't just diplomatic with your cybernetics. Suddenly your body can't tell the difference between the machine and the biological. You become a Cyber Psion. Cybernetics that have been installed are no longer separate pieces attached to you, they are accepted *as* you.

- **Prerequisites:** 2 Major Milestones already selected, Cyber Prothetical Advantage at least Rank 1, Rapid Healing Advantage at least rank 1

- **Benefit:** Cybernetics no longer need repair and regenerate like biological parts.

  - You gain the Addiction Disadvantage at Rank 2 for consuming raw Carbon to sustain your inorganic structures.

#### 3 Major Milestones Required

These Milestones require at least 3 Major Milestone to have already been acquired along with any other prerequisites.

**Iconic Weapon**

*Your Signature weapon becomes feared, respected, or whispered about in certain circles.*

- **Prerequisites:** 3 Major Milestone already taken + *Signature Weap*on milestone

- Upgrade it:

  - +1 Mod Slot (total 3)

  - +1 Upgrade (total 2)

- **Attunement:** Gain +5 on social skills (Deception, Intimidation, Persuasion, Seduction) when the weapon is visible.

**Can't See Me**

There are times when you can't afford to be seen. Some learn to hide well. Others learn to practically disappear. And they can do it with a strange, nearly supernatural kind of prowess. At this level you can hide your own aura from things that go bump in the night. Your heart rate slows keeping you calm, your aware of your surroundings enough instinctually that you're capable if knowing how predators hunt and where not to be at the right time.

- **Prerequisites**: 3 Major Milestones already Selected, Favored Skill: Stealth, Danger Sense Advantage at least Rank 1, Lucky at least Rank 1

- **Benefit**: When a Stealth Skill Check is called, you can instead do a WILL Essence Check (TN 8, TH3). If successfully, you are effectively invisible to those in your environment as you move through it. Anyone who tries to detect you must do a WILL Essence check of their own (TN is your WILL, TH is 3 + number of Hits when entering stealth). Example: if I successfully enter stealth and I had 4 hits, then if my WILL was 5, anyone trying to detect me would do a WILL Essence check at TN 5 TH 6.

  - Once you’ve entered stealth in this manner, even those with Aura sight cannot perceive you.

**God Tier**

Skills are honed over time and will always be of the utmost importance. Humanity is faced with death thus granting them a powerful incentive to do what no other being could imagine possible.

- **Prerequisites**: 3 Major Milestones, Selected Skill must be least 8 Ranks

- **Benefit**: The selected Skill has a +25 Modifier on it instead of the standard Rank + Primary Skill + Synergy Bonus

#### 4 Major Milestones Required

These Milestones require at least 4 Major Milestone to have already been acquired along with any other prerequisites.

#### 5+ Major Milestones Required

These Milestones require at least 5 or more Major Milestone to have already been acquired along with any other prerequisites.

**Legendary Weapon**

*Your Iconic weapon is more than gear - it’s a symbol. It might be mythologized in the streets or the LINK.*

- **Prerequisites:** 5+ Major Milestone already taken + *Iconic Weapon* milestone

- Upgrade it:

  - +1 Mod Slot (total 4)

  - +1 Upgrade (total 3)

- **Signature Effect:** A cinematic combat move or reactive ability once per session. Work with GM to define. Some examples are:

  - Vampiric weapon – Heal up to X per Y damage done

  - Phasing attack – Weapon bypasses cover and armor

  - Surestrike - Treat all 1’s as normal (not botch).

- **Attunement:** The weapon is now bound to your identity. Anyone trying to use it suffers significant penalties unless ritually attuned or part of your legacy. Work with GM to define (-5 penalty? Causes 1HL damage? Something significant)

### Vampire

Upyr, Dhampir, Strigoi, Jiangshi, Draugur, Vrykolakas…

Many names have been used to describe the creatures that rise from the grave, haunt the night, and subsist on the blood of the living. The most recognized, however, is **Vampire**.

With origins shrouded in mystery, possibly dating back to ancient Mesopotamia, the creatures now known as Vampires eventually spread across the Old World like a plague. Clan leaders, those who took the original blood oaths, carved out their own territories, establishing hunting grounds in what would become Europe, Asia, and North Africa.

Whenever a nest became too active, stories of unnatural beings prowling the darkness began to spread, giving rise to the rich folklore associated with Vampires. These legends led to widespread superstition giving rise to the use of apotropaics like garlic, wild rose branches, or Holy water. Vampires themselves encouraged these beliefs, even profiting from them by selling charms and fake remedies. These false protections gave humans a misguided sense of security - one that allowed Vampires to continue their hunts unchallenged.

The advent of modern industry and globalization allowed Vampires to spread further into the shadows, with transportation granting them access to the New World and all it had to offer—including a naïve and densely packed populace, ripe for the picking.

By the 20th century, Vampires had become a fixture in popular culture portrayed in literature, radio, and film. The widespread romanticization of their kind dulled human fear, allowing nests to operate with near impunity. Their long lives granted them vast wealth and influence, with many of the world’s great families having ties to one of the ancient bloodlines.

***Vampires in NYTE City***

In NYTE City, Vampires thrive in the shadows, concealed by the chaos of urban decay. Widespread drug use, homelessness, body augmentation, and an ever-expanding nightlife allow them to exist among mortals, so long as they feed discreetly. Few bat an eye when someone vanishes off the streets, and if a drug-addled cybernetic enforcer rips apart a grounder in a fit of rage, the public blames Fragmentation, not some supernatural predator hunting in the neon-lit night. 

While they remain hidden from public knowledge, Vampires are not hiding. They are waiting. The Unseen Court, a secretive governing body, ensures their kind stays in the shadows while exerting influence over corporations, criminal syndicates, and political figures. Vampires have woven themselves into the very fabric of NYTE City, letting them rule, hunt, and play at their leisure. 

***Physical Characteristics***

Vampires are not so different from the typical NYTE City resident…at least on the surface. Their predatory nature sets them apart, pushing them to be faster, stronger, and often more striking than mere mortals could ever hope to be. 

Their altered metabolism and strictly liquid diet ensure that even the most obese human will eventually transform into a lean, sculpted predator. Without a properly functioning circulatory system, their skin loses its warmth, taking on pallid shades of blue, gray, or violet where once a healthy flush held sway. 

When a Vampire hungers, their eyes take on a reddish sheen, a telltale sign of the bloodlust clawing at their restraint. The closer they come to losing control, the more feral their features become — a glimpse of the monster beneath the mask. 

Their fangs stay hidden. Their hunger does not show - until they choose to let it.

***Playing a Vampire***

A Vampire doesn’t enter NYTE City. They’ve always been in it – older than the towers, older than the corporations, older than most of the things that think they’re in charge. Whether you're newly turned and still learning what you are, or old blood finally stepping out of the shadows, the city has been waiting for you either way. You are undead. You consume blood to survive. Sunlight kills you and NYTE City, to its credit, never fully sees the sun.

Vampires are territorial by nature, and most maintain a connection to their sire or others of their bloodline: whether as allies, rivals, or reluctant kin. Many choose to live in tightly knit nests, staking claims over hunting grounds across the city. 

Though all Vampires must feed on the living, the method by which they do so is entirely up to you. Do you stalk the underground clubs and college mixers, luring victims away with charm and deception? Or do you prey upon the desperate: the lost, the forgotten, the ones no one will miss? Perhaps you’ve found ways to sidestep the hunt altogether, striking deals with blood banks or preying upon animals instead. 

Whatever path you choose, feeding is <u>not optional</u>. It is a constant, looming necessity, and managing your hunger will define much of your existence. 

### Werewolf

The city does not belong to humanity alone. Beneath the concrete, beyond the neon glow, there are things that hunt in the dark, things that have always been there. Among them are the Werewolves: predators not of malice, but of duty.

For as long as there have been people, there have been wolves in the shadows, watching, waiting, protecting. Not from mankind, but for mankind. From the things that lurk beyond the Veil, the things that would drag this world into something far worse than mere oblivion.

Not all Werewolves come from the same lineage. Some were born to it, raised in families who have carried the wolf-spirit for generations. Others were taken by it, their humanity shattered in a moment of supernatural awakening. And some? Some were made -- not by fate or nature, but by the greed of men who wished to control something they never truly understood.

***Werewolves in NYTE City***

Werewolves are just a myth in NYTE City. They don’t exist. If syndicates whisper of them, it is only in hushed rumors — urban legends of impossible killers, vanishing bodies, and something *other* moving through the city’s darkened veins. Corporations keep what they know under lock and key.

But they are there.

Trueborn watch from the shadows, steering events in ways that no one will ever notice. Unblooded wander the streets, their spirits guiding them to conflicts yet unseen. Forge Fangs patrol corporate kill-zones, ensuring their masters’ secrets remain hidden. They are not the rulers of the night. They are not the puppeteers behind the city’s power struggles. They are the knife in the dark, the last line of defense against things that humanity cannot, or should not, know about.

Because in the end, the city is not their enemy.

It is their *territory.*

***Physical Characteristics***

Most of the time, a Werewolf looks human. Moves human. Passes for human without effort.

Look closer and something gives it away. A stillness that doesn't belong, a gait that suggests a pursuit predator even on a crowded street, a quality of attention that feels less like awareness and more like assessment. The body tends toward lean, dense muscle regardless of lifestyle. The eyes catch light in ways that don't quite make sense.

When the shift comes, subtlety ends. The body rebuilds itself into something that was never meant to exist in the modern world: height pushing past eight feet, jaws elongating, heavy muscle layering over a frame that moments ago looked entirely ordinary. Coarse fur. Claws that can open a grounder like a tin can. A presence that triggers something ancient and animal in anyone nearby.

The beast is not a separate creature. It is the same person, with different priorities.

***Playing a Werewolf***

A Werewolf doesn't choose what they are. They choose what they do with it.

You move through NYTE City as a human - blending in, operating in the spaces between the city's factions, carrying a secret that would make most people run. Your connection to your tribe, your lineage, and the Veil shapes everything about how you engage with the world. Loyalty matters. Territory matters. The things you protect, even when no one knows you're protecting them, matter.

The beast is always there. It is not a weapon you draw cleanly and sheathe when the fight is done. It is an instinct, a pressure, a part of you that has its own opinions about how situations should be resolved. Learning to work with it rather than against it is the difference between a Werewolf who survives and one who becomes a problem the Trueborn have to clean up.

The city will give you reasons to let it out. It always does. The question is whether you decide when — or whether the city decides for you.

#### Campaign Power Scaling

Werewolf Campaign Power Scaling

| **Power Level**   | **Stat Bonus** | **Starting SFR** | **Rate of Use (RoU)** |
|-------------------|----------------|------------------|-----------------------|
| Street Level      | 1d4            | WILL x3 + 5      | 3                     |
| Heroic            | 1d4+1          | WILL x3 + 10     | 5                     |
| Shadows           | 1d4+2          | WILL x3 + 15     | 7                     |
| World Coming Down | 1d4+3          | WILL x3 + 20     | 9                     |

#### Baseline Traits

- Supernatural

  - **SFR** and **RoU**: Having a connection to the spirit, Werewolves gain access to Spiritual Force Rating (SFR) to fuel their powers. Each round, the amount of SFR you can spend at once is limited by your Rate of Use (RoU)

  - **Unable to Purchase Advantages**: Being supernatural grants you mighty power, but locks you out of advantages that normal humans use to level the playing field

- Werewolf form

  - Werewolves can transform into a beastly form that grants them access to boons as they channel their wolf spirit

  - Enhanced Stats while transformed

    - REF + 2

    - MOB + 2

    - BOD +4

  - Natural Weapons

    - Claws: Melee, Damage 8 + BOD

    - Fangs: Melee, Damage 10+ BOD

- Feral Instincts

  - Werewolves gain +2 to Awareness Skill checks around sight, smell, or hearing

  - While transformed, werewolves cannot make TECH-based Skill Checks

- Regeneration

  - Werewolves can regenerate 1 HL of damage per round, unless inflicted with Withering Damage (Such as from silver)

#### Archetype Specialization (Origin)

Every werewolf has an origin, where they came from. This could be a bloodline, or something you were forced into. Each Werewolf origin grants you unique powers.

##### Trueborn

The origins of Trueborn are not fully understood. Trueborn werewolves have always been lycanthrope. They have heritage, tradition, and family ties that bind them. These venerable creatures are long lived and have been around for many centuries, only being noticed during the early days of ancient Rome. It is believed that they were once entirely human but found themselves a communion with spirits who embodied the power, force, and will of the wolf. These spirits then bound themselves to curtained family bloodlines so they could pass the gift of lycanthropy down through many generations as the boon of their pact.

**Transformation**

Trueborn werewolves can transform at will by making a WILL Essence check (TN 7 TH 2). These transformations take 1 round; a botched Essence check will prevent you from attempting transformation for 1d4 rounds

While in werewolf form, you can transform back at will. You will also transform back if knocked unconscious or have lost more than 50% of your health as Withering Damage

**Lunar Phase Blessing (Starter Power)**

Trueborn Werewolves have an intrinsic connection to the moon, gaining specific boons during each phase of the moon. These boons are active during the corresponding week of the moon’s cycle.

| Moon Phase | Boon | Effect | Description |
|----|----|----|----|
| New Moon | Shroud of Shadows | +2 to Stealth and Deception Skill Checks | The darkness of the new moon cloaks you in shadow, aiding in hiding your movement |
| Waxing Moon | Hunter’s Edge | +1 REF and BOD | The growing strength of the waxing moon sharpens your predatory instincts |
| Full Moon | Apex Fury | For 3 SFR: gain +2 REF, BOD, and MOB until unconscious or reducing to 50% Health | The moon’s power surges through you. Unleash your might |
| Waning Moon | Resilient Spirit | Natural Armor treated as Warding | The waning moon bolsters your spiritual endurance, allowing you to weather any storm |
